subject: Proposal: Hybrid liability cap architecture for Order Form — decision requested
body:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Hybrid liability cap architecture for Order Form — decision requested

Team —

Following our redline call with Nimbus earlier today, they pushed back on a single-contractwide cap as being too punitive for multi-year prepay structures. They specifically asked that any cap reflect a) fees actually paid (not forecasted ARR) and b) some protection for large one-off incidents (they asked for a per-incident floor).

High-level proposal for the Order Form redline (attached PDF + MSA draft):
- Total liability cap: greater of (i) 1x fees paid in the prior 12 months; or (ii) $1.5M absolute floor.
- Per-incident exposure cap: capped at 0.5x fees paid in the prior 12 months for any single incident (so incidents cannot exhaust the lifetime cap in one event).
- Exclusions/carve-outs: IP indemnity, willful misconduct, and gross negligence remain outside the cap. Confidentiality breach limited to direct remediation costs; consequential damages excluded (standard carve).
- Measurement basis: use billed fees on invoice history (credits/refunds netted), not ARR or committed spend.

Rationale: this hybrid approach keeps an aggregate ceiling but prevents distortion where a large prepayment front-loads exposure. It gives legal a clear calculation and sales a defensible commercial position.

Requesting: legal sign-off on the specific language (see MSA_redline_v3.docx) and approval for sales to offer this construct to Nimbus as our preferred compromise. If legal prefers a different multiplier (1x vs 2x), note impact to pricing/credits.

Thanks,
Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Director, Commercial Deals | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

---

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Hybrid liability cap architecture for Order Form — decision requested

Laura —

Looks sensible to me. Two quick commercial notes:
1) Nimbus is already asking for credits for early termination in year 1; if we move to a 1x billed-fees cap that will significantly increase their upside in a breach scenario. We should flag potential margin impact to pricing/sales concessions.
2) We should pre-clear the per-incident carve to avoid ambiguity around cumulative incidents vs separate cause events (customer may try to slice incidents to maximize recovery).

If legal is comfortable with "billed fees" as the measurement, I'm OK to push.

-J

> Laura / Jordan —
>
> Suggestion from ops: make the measurement window a "rolling 12-month" rather than "prior 12 months" tied to contract start. That avoids gaming from upfront prepayments followed by immediate incidents.
>
> Also +1 on being explicit about credits/discounts being netted out.
>
> Marcus

>--
>Marcus Lin
>Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

> 2) per-incident carve parameters so it's not interpreted as "each outage = full cap".

On Sun, Apr 4, 2027 at 08:45 AM Elena Morris <elena.morris@nimbus-analytics.com> wrote:

> Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
> Subject: Re: Nimbus feedback on cap proposal
>
> Thanks Stephanie —
>
> Appreciate the draft. Nimbus' position (per GC) is that an annualized cap can be punitive where customers prepay multi-year commitments. Our ask is specifically: 2x fees paid in the prior 12 months OR a clear rolling-12 approach, whichever produces a higher cap. We will not accept an absolute dollar floor unless the vendor can show why that better aligns incentives.
>
> For per-incident language: our preference is a separate per-incident cap equal to 0.5x fees paid in the prior 12 months. That prevents a single event from consuming the customer's entire remedy budget. We are open to keeping IP and wilful-misconduct carve-outs outside the cap.
>
> Happy to discuss — we have midday availability tomorrow.
>
> Best,
>Elena

On Sun, Apr 4, 2027 at 09:30 AM Alex Rivera <arivera@tidehilllegal.com> wrote:

> From: Alex Rivera <arivera@tidehilllegal.com>
> To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
> Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -0700
> Subject: Re: Nimbus feedback on cap proposal

> Laura / Marcus —
>
> Quick counsel perspective for your negotiation playbook: the two levers you can trade are (1) multiplier on fees (1x vs 2x) and (2) whether the basis is billed fees vs committed spend/ARR. If you're trying to preserve liability discipline, keeping the multiplier at 1x but using rolling 12-month billed fees is cleaner and defensible. A 2x multiple materially increases vendor exposure and would require commercial offset (price increase or higher credit reserve).
>
> If Redwood wants a dollar floor, tie it to a cap-tier based on contract value (e.g., $1.5M for contracts <$5M, $3M for contracts >= $5M) rather than a flat floor. That keeps alignment across deal sizes.
>
> Also recommend explicit language on netting credits and on how refunds are treated for the measurement period.
>
> Alex Rivera
>Tidehill Legal (outside counsel for Nimbus)
>arivera@tidehilllegal.com
